meta.description: Process many sequence files in batch (count, merge, split, convert, summarize) with memory-safe streaming and on-disk indexing using Biopython, pysam, or pyfastx. Use when iterating over a directory of FASTA/FASTQ files, merging or splitting datasets, building random access across many or huge files, or automating per-file operations without exhausting RAM.

scientific_integrity.detail: No output fabricated sequence counts, identifiers, quality values, studies, sample sizes, p-values, or efficacy data; all numerical results came from retained public fixtures or bounded generated records.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill performs sequence-file engineering and makes no patient-specific diagnostic, treatment, or clinical recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: Streaming, persistent indexing, deterministic traversal, format-loss, and Phred+33 versus Phred+64 guidance were methodologically correct in all five independent cases.

code_usability.detail: All three Python files parsed; every accessible advertised function and both CLIs executed; fork and spawn paths agreed; the shipped 11-test suite passed with ResourceWarning fatal.

functional_suitability.note: Count, merge, split, conversion, summary, persistent indexing, thin-reader, gzip-index, and parallel workflows are complete and independently correct.

reliability.note: Major invalid and partial-operation states are explicit and recoverable; record-count split destinations remain caller-managed rather than manifest-backed.

performance_context.note: Progressive references, streaming iteration, persistent indexes, bounded chunks, and bounded prefix handles match the high-volume scope.

agent_usability.note: Routing, outputs, safety checks, and error prevention are clear; recursive summary and worker rows use basenames, which can make duplicate nested names ambiguous.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language, explicit workflow choices, readable outputs, and actionable failure checks support both discovery and recovery.

security.note: No credentials or raw-code execution are present; untrusted ID prefixes, reserved names, containment, case collisions, and overwrite safety are enforced.

maintainability.note: The package is modular, deterministic, and covered by 11 focused regressions plus independently callable public functions.

agent_specific.note: Triggering, progressive disclosure, composition, and stop conditions are strong; read-only paths are repeatable and prefix outputs intentionally refuse overwrite, while count-split output reuse is caller-controlled.

inputs.label: Count, merge, split, index, convert, and standalone demo
inputs.note: Two fresh FASTA inputs produced checked counts, stable merge order, 3/1 and 2/2/1 splits, a seven-record reopened index, 94 converted public records, and the documented standalone values.

assertions.text: Streaming counts and stable merge preserve all records in deterministic order.
assertions.note: Counts were three and four; the merged output contained seven records in a.fasta then b.fasta order.

assertions.text: Two fresh record-count splits are bounded and lossless.
assertions.note: Four records split as 3/1 and five records split as 2/2/1 with every chunk parsed back.

assertions.text: Persistent multi-file indexing survives close and reopen with exact lookup values.
assertions.note: The reopened SQLite index contained seven records and preserved the checked a2 and b3 sequence lengths.

assertions.text: GenBank-to-FASTA conversion preserves record count and sequence while the documentation warns about annotation loss.
assertions.note: All 94 public orchid records converted; the checked first identifier and sequence matched the GenBank source.

assertions.text: The standalone demonstration is runnable and emits readable checked values.
assertions.note: It exited zero and reported 5/5/5 records, three chunks, 15 indexed records, and lookup length 52.

inputs.label: pyfastx gzip reuse and pysam quality semantics
inputs.note: The function and CLI reused one gzip FASTA index for 94 records and checked lengths 740/592/740; public Phred+33 values matched and a legacy quality demonstrated the documented 71 versus 40 interpretation boundary.

assertions.text: The importable pyfastx function builds a persistent gzip FASTA index and returns meaningful record metadata.
assertions.note: It indexed 94 records and returned checked first/last selected lengths of 740 and 592.

assertions.text: Function reuse and CLI reuse preserve the same persistent index.
assertions.note: The .fxi hash and inode were unchanged across the second function call and CLI invocation.

assertions.text: The CLI output is valid JSON and agrees with function-level random access.
assertions.note: The CLI reported 94 records and selected length 740 for the checked identifier.

assertions.text: pysam thin FASTQ parsing agrees with explicit Biopython parsing for Phred+33 data.
assertions.note: Three public reads, the first sequence, and its quality array matched; the first range was 18 to 26.

assertions.text: The documented legacy Phred+64 caveat is scientifically observable rather than merely stated.
assertions.note: ASCII h was 71 under pysam's fixed subtraction of 33 and 40 under Biopython fastq-illumina parsing.

inputs.label: Empty summaries and invalid chunk/worker bounds
inputs.note: No-match and empty-file summaries were explicit; six invalid chunk values and four invalid worker values failed actionably, and the valid split remained 2/2/1.

assertions.text: No-match summary output is a valid header-only CSV with the complete public schema.
assertions.note: The result was [] and the exact columns were file,sequences,total_bp,min_len,max_len,avg_len.

assertions.text: An empty FASTA produces explicit, readable zero metrics rather than a crash or blank file.
assertions.note: The row identified empty.fasta and returned zero for all five numerical measures.

assertions.text: Invalid chunk sizes fail before input access or output creation with an actionable parameter message.
assertions.note: False, True, 0, -1, 1.5, and '2' all raised the stable positive-integer ValueError against a deliberately missing input without filesystem changes.

assertions.text: A valid boundary split remains lossless after validation was added.
assertions.note: Five records parsed back as chunks 2, 2, and 1.

assertions.text: Invalid multiprocessing worker counts are rejected before pool construction.
assertions.note: Zero, negative, Boolean, and floating-point worker counts all raised the stable positive-integer error.

inputs.label: Contained prefix splitting under hostile and high-cardinality inputs
inputs.note: Traversal, reserved names, manifest escape, existing target, and case collision were safely rejected; 2,048 prefixes completed under a 32-descriptor limit with max_open_files=8 and no descriptor growth.

assertions.text: Record-derived paths cannot escape the output directory or alter an existing sibling.
assertions.note: The ../ prefix was rejected, the sibling sentinel was byte-preserved, and the partial manifest recorded zero writes.

assertions.text: Reserved filenames and manifest path traversal are rejected before unsafe output is created.
assertions.note: CON was rejected and ../escaped.json could not leave the output directory.

assertions.text: Existing targets are never overwritten and case-insensitive collisions are explicitly accounted.
assertions.note: The existing target sentinel remained unchanged; Sample/sample stopped with a one-record partial manifest.

assertions.text: Open handles remain bounded while all 2,048 distinct prefixes are written and parseable.
assertions.note: Under RLIMIT_NOFILE=32 and max_open_files=8, manifest rows, count sum, output-file count, and parsed records all equaled 2,048; descriptors were 4 before and after.

assertions.text: Reopening an evicted prefix appends without truncating earlier records.
assertions.note: The interleaved a group parsed back as a_1 then a_2 with four total records across the manifest.

inputs.label: Creation-order determinism and fork/spawn parity
inputs.note: Opposite creation histories yielded a.fasta,z/a.fasta,z/B.fasta and byte-identical summaries/merges; fork, spawn, and spawn rerun agreed on stable rows, six records, and 15 bp. Basename-only row identifiers remain a minor recursive-readability limitation.

assertions.text: Opposite filesystem creation histories produce the same documented relative-path order.
assertions.note: Both trees resolved to a.fasta, z/a.fasta, z/B.fasta using the casefolded/exact stable key.

assertions.text: Summary output is row-stable and byte-identical across creation histories.
assertions.note: Rows matched and both CSV files had SHA-256 baf79636270cad3d4a4f4442eb03eee6cfe3fb06188ad3f7f460d6ddcdafcb79.

assertions.text: Streaming merge output is record-stable and byte-identical across creation histories.
assertions.note: Both six-record merges had SHA-256 fa38059609575f34feb44e5e3ddc886f976ae7549b7993a5c394e393a4f9dd3f.

assertions.text: Real two-worker fork and spawn execution return identical stable results.
assertions.note: Fork, spawn, and a second spawn run returned the same three ordered rows.

assertions.text: Parallel results preserve complete checked totals across start methods.
assertions.note: Every run reported six records and 15 total base pairs; duplicate nested basenames did not alter values or order.

key_strengths: Untrusted sequence identifiers are separated from filesystem paths through portable-prefix validation, resolved containment, case-collision detection, and exclusive creation.
The prefix splitter completed 2,048 outputs under a 32-descriptor limit with exact manifest and parsed totals and no descriptor growth.
Every multi-file path is deterministically ordered, and real fork/spawn/rerun results plus summary and merge bytes agreed across opposite creation histories.
Biopython, pysam, and pyfastx routes were executed against retained public fixtures with exact count, random-access, conversion, and quality-encoding checks.

recommendations.title: BATCH-008: Preserve relative paths in recursive rows
recommendations.problem: summarize_files and process_file emit Path.name, so recursively discovered files with the same basename produce stable but visually ambiguous row identifiers.
recommendations.root_cause: The public result schema was designed for flat directories and does not accept or retain a caller root for relative-path labels.
recommendations.fix: In a future compatible polish pass, accept an optional label root or input-label mapping and emit reviewed relative POSIX paths while preserving the current flat-directory default. Add a duplicate-basename recursive regression.
